# GR-01 Re-review 2 — H1 MSP Promotion Readiness

**Review date:** 2026-08-10
**Reviewer:** Fresh independent read-only re-reviewer
**Review target:** `GR-01-h1-readiness.md` after fix cycle 2
**Status:** COMPLETE

**Verdict: `WARN`** — all three prior hard findings are corrected and the H1
writer verdict `NEEDS_REVISION` remains evidence-backed. One non-blocking document-control
warning remains: the reviewed H1 report does not identify its version, review date, or
writer/reviewer in its own header.

## Review boundary and non-action record

This review re-read the GR-01 brief, current H1 report, original review, Re-review 1, the L0
atomic index, the two Visual Office inbound proposals, the other pending ADR-068 envelope,
canonical ADR-068, the Phase 2 contract, H1/EV-GOV-001 plan evidence, the MSP scripts/runbook,
and current RBAC/session sources. `gks/00_index/atomic_index.jsonl` was read before the selected
Phase 2 note. No proposal, canonical note, index, script, code, schema, generated target, or
Git state was changed. The only file written by this review is this report.

The module names `auth-config.js` and `auth.js` (module proposal line 24) but provides no Phase 3 blueprint or inferred provenance. The amendment makes current-matrix/`withAuth` claims (lines 31 and 45) and uses `documented_source`, not `inferred`, at `confidence: 0.9` (lines 20–22). This matches the warning rule in the contract (lines 134–136), without claiming the unavailable inbound validator’s L1 disposition. |
| F-02 — update-version treatment | **FIXED** | The H1 report correctly distinguishes conditional required fields from the update constraint (lines 49 and 56–61). `version` is conditionally required only for `module`, `feature`, and `protocol` (contract lines 27–37), not `architecture_decision`; the amendment’s required `context_anchor.duration` and `epistemic.confidence` are present (amendment lines 18–21). `no_invented_versions` constrains an existing-note version change to SemVer (contract lines 126–128); it does not require this ADR amendment to supply a version. The report correctly says that any changed final canonical version must be a SemVer increment from the baseline selected after same-target reconciliation (lines 71–74, 147–149). |
| F-03 — same-target conflict evidence | **FIXED** | The H1 report cites the other inbound envelope and records the exact collision (lines 127–133). The Visual Office amendment declares `target_file: gks/phase2_atomic/ADR-068-persona-based-rbac.md` at line 4, identically to `20260809090000-claude-opus-5-update_atomic-adr068-pos-tenant-domains.md` line 4. Human/MSP ordering or reconciliation is therefore required before a final ADR-068 result is selected. |

## Merge semantics and command boundary

The `update_atomic` proposal type means only “modify existing file” (contract lines 146–161).
Neither the contract nor the reviewed tooling defines a partial-patch representation, inherited
frontmatter, insertion point, or deterministic conflict/section merge. The canonical-only
validator reads `gks/phase2_atomic/` and writes a validation report/meta artifact
(`scripts/msp/validate-atomic-ids.mjs` lines 9–11, 34–38, 122–148); it is not an inbound
merge validator. `_merge-adr-collision.mjs` is explicitly a one-shot ADR-057…061 repair
(`scripts/msp/_merge-adr-collision.mjs` lines 2–18, 41–44), not a promotion mechanism.

Accordingly, `npm run msp:validate`, `npm run msp:index`, and `npm run msp:check` remain
available but were correctly not run by the H1 report: each operates on or writes canonical
index/validation state, and none supplies inbound acceptance. The autonomous-gates runbook
also does not authorize a Phase 2 promotion; it never merges and its successful endpoint is a
draft PR (`docs/runbooks/codex-autonomous-gates.md` lines 5–8).

## Gate position

The reviewed report’s `NEEDS_REVISION` verdict is retained. Before promotion, a human/MSP
reviewer must reconcile/order the two ADR-068 updates and approve a complete, non-lossy final
ADR (or an MSP-approved deterministic merge procedure), with a SemVer-valid version only if the
final canonical ADR changes it. MSP acceptance and canonical L0 index proof are still required
to close H1. This re-review authorizes none of promotion, indexing, code work, deployment, or
runtime capability change.
